title: Kangla was the traditional seat of Manipuri rule
text: Kangla was the historic seat of the rulers of Manipur and the ceremonial centre of the valley. After the colonial period it was used as a military and administrative post, and it was formally handed back to the people of Manipur in November 2004, when it reopened as a heritage site.

title: The site is laid out around moats and ceremonial gateways
text: The complex is organised around water: moats, ponds and the nearby Imphal river. Ceremonial gateways, temple platforms and open lawns mark the ritual and political functions the site once held.

title: The Kangla Sha are the guardian figures of the site
text: Two large sculpted figures of a mythical lion like creature, the Kangla Sha, stand within the complex. They are among the most recognised symbols of Manipuri heritage and appear widely in state iconography.

title: The name is traditionally explained as dry land
text: The name Kangla is traditionally explained in Meitei as dry land, referring to ground that stood clear of the surrounding wetland. This is a traditional explanation rather than a settled academic conclusion.

title: Plan around ninety minutes, more with a guide
text: Most visitors spend ninety minutes to two hours on site. Entry and timings are managed by the site authority and are worth checking on the day, particularly around commemorations.

title: The market is run entirely by women traders
text: Ima Keithel, the mothers market, is operated by women traders. The number of traders runs into the thousands across the market halls, covering handloom, fresh produce, fish, household goods and prepared food.

title: The market is connected to the Nupi Lan movements
text: The women traders of the market were central to the Nupi Lan, the women agitations of 1904 and 1939 against colonial era economic measures. The market is therefore a political landmark as much as a commercial one.

title: Go in the morning and buy directly
text: The market is busiest and most photogenic in the morning. Buying handloom directly from the trader keeps the value with the household that wove it. Ask before photographing a stall.

title: Loktak is the largest freshwater lake in the region
text: Loktak is the largest freshwater lake in northeast India and the defining feature of the Manipur valley drainage. Its surface area varies through the year with rainfall and water management.

title: Phumdi are floating mats of vegetation, soil and organic matter
text: The floating islands of Loktak, called phumdi, are heterogeneous masses of vegetation, soil and organic matter in different stages of decomposition. They are thick enough to walk on in places and to build on in others.

title: The circular rings are fish enclosures built by fishers
text: The regular circles visible in aerial photographs are athaphum, artificial phumdi rings built by fishing households to enclose and concentrate fish. They are a livelihood technique, not a natural formation.

title: Loktak is a designated wetland of international importance
text: Loktak was designated a Ramsar site in 1990 in recognition of its international importance as a wetland, and was later placed on the Montreux Record, which lists sites where ecological character is changing or is likely to change.

title: Water level management is the central conservation question
text: Barrage operation downstream holds water levels more constant than the natural seasonal cycle. The consequences for phumdi thickness, fish stocks and the habitat at Keibul Lamjao are an active subject of study and debate.

title: Loktak Lake is about 48 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: The lake is located in Bishnupur district. It is approximately 48 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, and the drive usually takes around 1 to 1.5 hours depending on traffic.

title: Go at sunrise and dress for the water
text: The lake is at its best in the hour after sunrise, when the light is low and the water is still. Mornings between November and February are cold on open water, so carry a windproof layer even on a clear day.

title: The park is the last natural habitat of the Sangai
text: Keibul Lamjao is the last natural habitat of the Sangai, the brow antlered deer that is the state animal of Manipur. The species is listed as endangered and its range is effectively limited to this wetland.

title: The habitat itself floats
text: The park is described as the only floating national park of its kind because the deer live on phumdi rather than on solid ground. The animals move across a mat that rises and falls with the water level.

title: Protection was formalised in stages
text: The area was given sanctuary protection in 1966 and was declared a national park in 1977, in response to the very small surviving population of the deer.

title: Early morning gives the best chance of a sighting
text: Sightings are most likely soon after dawn from the watchtowers. Carry binoculars, keep noise down, and accept that a sighting is never guaranteed in a wild population this small.

title: The INA flag was raised at Moirang in April 1944
text: On 14 April 1944 the flag of the Indian National Army was raised at Moirang during the Imphal campaign of the Second World War. The site is commemorated by a memorial complex and museum.

title: Moirang is the setting of the Khamba and Thoibi tradition
text: Moirang is closely associated with the story of Khamba and Thoibi, a love narrative central to Manipuri literature, dance and ritual, and connected to the Thangjing shrine. It is transmitted as tradition and performance rather than as documented event history.

title: Pair it with Loktak in one half day
text: Moirang sits on the same road as the Loktak viewpoints, so the memorial complex and the lake work well as a single half day rather than two separate trips.

title: Ukhrul is the home district of the Tangkhul Naga community
text: Ukhrul is the headquarters of the district of the same name and the principal home of the Tangkhul Naga community, with its own language, weaving traditions, agricultural calendar and village governance practices.

title: The town sits high enough to change the weather completely
text: Ukhrul lies in the eastern hills at roughly sixteen hundred to nineteen hundred metres, which makes it markedly cooler than the Imphal valley and gives the district its terraced agriculture and pine slopes.

title: Luira Phanit opens the agricultural year
text: Luira Phanit, the seed sowing festival, marks the start of the Tangkhul agricultural year and is among the most significant occasions in the district calendar, with dance, song and community feasting.

title: Village visits are hosted, not open access
text: Village life in the district is organised around community authority. Visits work best when they are arranged through a local host or guide, which is also what routes visitor spending to the households involved.

title: Allow three to four hours from Imphal
text: Ukhrul is roughly eighty kilometres from Imphal by road, but the hill route means three to four hours in practice. Travel in daylight and check road conditions in the monsoon.

title: The Shirui lily grows on one hill range and nowhere else
text: Lilium mackliniae, the Shirui lily, is found in the wild on the Shirui hill range in Ukhrul district and effectively nowhere else. It is the state flower of Manipur and is listed as endangered.

title: It was described for science in 1946 and named after a wife
text: The lily was brought to scientific attention by the botanist Frank Kingdon-Ward in 1946, and the species name mackliniae honours his wife, Jean Macklin. Local communities had of course known the plant long before that.

title: The flowering window is short and the habitat is fragile
text: Flowering is concentrated in May and June. Because the habitat is restricted and the slope is easily damaged, visitor pressure in that window is the single biggest management question for the site.

title: Stay on the path and do not pick
text: Walk on marked routes, do not pick or transplant the flowers, and go with a local guide. The state holds an annual Shirui Lily Festival, which is also the busiest time on the hill.

title: Andro pottery is made without a wheel
text: Potters at Andro shape vessels by hand using coiling and beating rather than a wheel, a technique passed down within households. The clay and the firing method give the finished pieces their characteristic surface.

title: The village keeps a tradition of a continuously maintained fire
text: Andro is associated with a tradition of a sacred fire kept continuously alight. It is maintained and explained by the community as a living practice rather than as a documented historical record.

title: About an hour east of Imphal
text: Andro is roughly twenty five kilometres east of Imphal and works as a half day trip. Buying directly from the artisan households is the most effective way to support the craft.

title: The battle of 23 April 1891 was the final stand
text: The Battle of Khongjom on 23 April 1891 was the last major resistance of the Anglo-Manipuri War. Major Paona Brajabasi is the figure most closely associated with the stand made on Kheba hill.

title: Khongjom Day is observed every year on 23 April
text: Khongjom Day is observed annually on 23 April as a state commemoration, and the memorial complex is the focus of the observance.

title: The cemetery commemorates the 1944 Imphal campaign
text: The Imphal War Cemetery holds the graves of Commonwealth personnel who died in the fighting around Imphal in 1944. It is maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission.

title: It anchors a wider battlefield circuit
text: The cemetery is usually visited together with the Moirang memorial and other sites connected to the 1944 campaign, forming a circuit that attracts specialist visitors from outside the region.

title: The valley sits on the Manipur and Nagaland boundary
text: Dzukou valley lies at roughly two thousand four hundred metres on the boundary between Manipur and Nagaland, and is reached on foot from either side.

title: Dry season fire is the main risk to the valley
text: The ground cover that makes the valley distinctive is also highly combustible in the dry months, and the valley has suffered damaging fires. Open flame discipline is the most important rule for any visitor.

title: Treat it as a full day with a guide
text: The approach involves a sustained climb and the weather changes quickly. Go with a guide, start early, carry water and warm layers, and carry all waste back out.

title: Tamenglong is a major stop for migrating Amur falcons
text: The district is an internationally significant roosting site for Amur falcons on their migration, and community led protection has become a widely cited conservation success in the region.

title: The district is known for its oranges
text: Tamenglong oranges are well known in the region and are celebrated with an annual orange festival, which is the busiest visitor period in an otherwise quiet district.

title: Visitor infrastructure is still thin
text: Waterfalls, caves and lake sites are spread out and the approaches are unpaved. Accommodation is limited and largely informal, which is why the district is treated as a development candidate rather than a promotion target.

title: The temple is generally dated to the fifteenth century
text: The Vishnu temple at Bishnupur is generally dated to the fifteenth century and is a protected monument. Its brick construction and form are often read as showing influence from beyond the valley.

title: It is a five minute stop on the Loktak road
text: The temple sits directly on the route most visitors already take towards Loktak, so adding it costs very little time and spreads visitor attention across more of the district.

title: Moreh faces Tamu across the international border
text: Moreh sits on the India and Myanmar border opposite the town of Tamu, and its markets and mixed population reflect a long history of cross border trade.

title: Access depends on current regulations
text: What visitors may do at and near the border changes with prevailing regulations and advisories. Any promotion of Moreh has to be checked against the position on the day rather than assumed from earlier practice.

title: Kangla is about 8 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Kangla Fort is located in the heart of Imphal city. It is approximately 8 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, and the drive usually takes around 20 minutes.

title: Ima Keithel is about 8 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Ima Keithel is situated centrally in Imphal. It is roughly 8 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, taking about 20 to 25 minutes by taxi or auto-rickshaw.

title: Keibul Lamjao is about 53 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in Bishnupur district. It is approximately 53 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, with a driving time of around 1.5 hours.

title: Moirang is about 45 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Moirang is situated in Bishnupur district. It is about 45 kilometres south of Imphal International Airport, usually taking around 1 hour and 15 minutes by road.

title: Ukhrul is about 83 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Ukhrul town is located in the eastern hills. It is approximately 83 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, and the winding hill drive takes around 2.5 to 3 hours.

title: Shirui is about 95 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Shirui Peak is situated beyond Ukhrul town. It is approximately 95 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, requiring a drive of about 3 to 3.5 hours.

title: Andro is about 25 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: The cultural village of Andro is located in Imphal East district. It is roughly 25 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, and the drive takes about 45 to 50 minutes.

title: Khongjom is about 35 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Khongjom War Memorial is located in Thoubal district. It is approximately 35 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, generally taking around 1 hour by road.

title: Moreh is about 110 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: The border town of Moreh is in Tengnoupal district. It is roughly 110 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, and the hill drive takes approximately 3.5 to 4 hours.

title: Imphal War Cemetery is about 8 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: The Imphal War Cemetery is located in the central part of the city. It is approximately 8 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, a short drive of about 20 minutes.

title: The Dzukou Valley trek base is about 100 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: The trekking base for Dzukou Valley on the Manipur side is in Senapati district, roughly 100 kilometres from Imphal International Airport. The drive takes about 3 hours before the trek begins.

title: Tamenglong is about 150 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: Tamenglong is a western hill district. It is approximately 150 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, and the challenging hill drive takes around 5 to 6 hours.

title: Bishnupur Temple is about 30 kilometres from Imphal Airport
text: The historic Bishnupur Temple is on the route to Loktak Lake. It is roughly 30 kilometres from Imphal International Airport, taking about 45 minutes to reach by car.
